title: Erdős Problem #1041: Paths in Polynomial Level Sets
description: For a monic polynomial with all roots in the unit disk, must there exist a path of length less than 2 in the sublevel set {z : |f(z)| < 1} connecting two roots?

overview.historicalContext:
This problem originates from the 1958 paper 'Metric properties of polynomials' by Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian. They studied the geometry of polynomial level sets—specifically the sublevel set {z : |f(z)| < 1} for monic polynomials with roots in the unit disk.

The authors proved that this sublevel set always has a connected component containing at least two roots (the Component Lemma). The open problem asks for a quantitative strengthening: can we find not just connectivity, but a SHORT path of length less than 2 connecting two roots?

The constant 2 is sharp—it's the diameter of the unit disk, so roots could be nearly 2 apart. The conjecture asks whether the sublevel set always provides an efficient shortcut.
overview.problemStatement:
Let $f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{n}(z - z_i) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ be a monic polynomial with $|z_i| < 1$ for all $i$.

**Conjecture (OPEN)**: Must there always exist a path of length less than $2$ in the sublevel set
$$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |f(z)| < 1\}$$
which connects two of the roots of $f$?

**Known** (Erdős-Herzog-Piranian 1958): The sublevel set always has a connected component containing at least two roots.
overview.text: For a monic polynomial with all roots in the unit disk, must there exist a path of length less than 2 in the sublevel set {z : |f(z)| < 1} connecting two roots?
overview.proofStrategy:
We formalize this problem by:

1. **Defining sublevel sets**: `sublevelSet f r = {z : ‖f.eval z‖ < r}`

2. **Defining path length**: Using 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1]`

3. **Stating the Component Lemma**: The known 1958 result about connected components

4. **Stating the main conjecture**: Existence of a path of length < 2

5. **Special cases**: The quadratic case as a base case

6. **Properties**: Sublevel sets are open and contain all roots
keyInsights: **Sublevel sets are open**: Since polynomial evaluation is continuous, {z : |f(z)| < 1} is an open set containing all roots.
**Why 2 is the bound**: The diameter of the unit disk is 2, so any two roots are at distance less than 2. The conjecture asks if the sublevel set provides a path achieving this.
**Component vs path**: The Component Lemma guarantees connectivity but not path length. A winding path through the sublevel set could be arbitrarily long.
**Lemniscates**: The level curves {z : |f(z)| = c} are called polynomial lemniscates. They have beautiful geometric properties studied since Bernoulli.
**Quadratic base case**: For degree 2, the straight line segment between roots lies in the sublevel set and has length < 2.

conclusion.summary: We formalize Erdős Problem #1041 about paths in polynomial sublevel sets. The Erdős-Herzog-Piranian Component Lemma (1958) shows that the sublevel set {z : |f(z)| < 1} has a connected component containing at least two roots. The open conjecture asks whether this connected component contains a SHORT path of length less than 2 connecting two roots.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This problem connects complex analysis, metric geometry, and potential theory.

Understanding the geometry of polynomial level sets has applications in numerical analysis (root-finding algorithms) and complex dynamics. The 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure provides the natural notion of path length for potentially irregular curves.
openQuestions: Does the conjecture hold for all monic polynomials with roots in the unit disk?
What is the supremum of the minimal path length over all such polynomials?
Is there a relationship between degree n and the minimal achievable path length?
Can the conjecture be strengthened to require the straight-line segment lies in the sublevel set?

crossReferences.description: Erdős #1040 studies transfinite diameter and the measure of sublevel sets for monic polynomials with roots in the unit disk — the same setting as #1041, examining the potential-theoretic capacity of {z : |f(z)| < 1}.

Erdős #1042 asks about connected components of polynomial lemniscates {z : |f(z)| = c}, the level curves bounding the sublevel sets studied in #1041. The Component Lemma from 1041 directly motivates the finer lemniscate topology questions in #1042.
Erdős #1039 concerns the disc radius of polynomial lemniscates for monic polynomials with roots in the unit disk. The same polynomial family and level-set geometry underlies both problems.

Erdős #1044 asks for bounds on the boundary length of polynomial level sets. Short-path existence inside sublevel sets (#1041) and bounds on the bounding curve's length (#1044) are complementary metric questions about polynomial level-set geometry.

Erdős #1038 studies sublevel sets of monic polynomials from a measure-theory perspective, forming part of the same cluster of Erdős–Herzog–Piranian problems on the geometry and measure of polynomial sublevel sets.

relatedProofs.description: The Component Lemma proved in #1041 (at least two roots in a single connected component of {z : |f(z)| < 1}) is the departure point for the lemniscate connectivity questions formalized in #1042.
Erdős #1043 examines projections of polynomial level sets. Together with #1041, these problems form a systematic study of the metric and topological properties of polynomial level-set geometry.

Erdős #1045 studies the maximum product of distances from points in the unit disk to the roots — a quantity closely related to |f(z)| for monic polynomials. Extremal configurations for that problem overlap with those relevant to short-path questions.

references.title: Metric properties of polynomials
references.description: The foundational paper establishing the Component Lemma: for any monic polynomial with roots in the unit disk, the sublevel set {z : |f(z)| < 1} has a connected component containing at least two roots. This is the starting point for Erdős Problem #1041.

references.title: On the length of lemniscates
references.description: Proves that the total length of the lemniscate {z : |f(z)| = 1} for a degree-n monic polynomial is O(n), with sharp constants. This work informs quantitative path-length questions inside sublevel sets.

references.title: The area of polynomial lemniscates
references.journal: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
references.description: Studies the area enclosed by polynomial lemniscates and its relation to the capacity of the polynomial. Provides potential-theoretic tools complementary to the path-length approach of Erdős Problem #1041.

references.title: A conjecture of Erdős on the connectivity of lemniscates
references.description: Discusses connectivity properties of polynomial lemniscates, directly engaging with the Erdős–Herzog–Piranian framework and related open problems including the short-path conjecture.

references.title: Logarithmic Potentials with External Fields
references.description: Standard reference on logarithmic potential theory and polynomial lemniscates. Chapter III covers transfinite diameter, capacity, and the geometry of level sets — the potential-theoretic backbone for the Erdős sublevel-set problems.
